answer.part: How rule is determined, including ties, tokens, and Vagabond
answer.ruling: A player rules a clearing with more total warriors plus buildings than each other player; tokens and pawns do not count. Ordinary ties mean nobody rules. Eyrie win ties for most if they have at least one Eyrie piece there. Vagabond cannot rule or prevent another player from ruling.
answer.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle (Rule 2.5)

answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle

answer.part: Legal normal move, repeated movement, and rivers
answer.ruling: Move any positive number of your warriors/pawns from one clearing along a linking path to an adjacent clearing. You must rule the origin, destination, or both, and recheck rule for each move. The same pieces may move repeatedly, including on multiple moves in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly treats them as paths.
answer.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle; Move (4.2)

answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle; Move

answer.part: Battle from ambush through removal
answer.ruling: Choose a clearing containing your warriors or pawn and an enemy defender; battle does not require ruling. Defender may play a matching ambush (birds wild); attacker may foil with matching ambush. If not foiled, defender deals two immediate hits, not limited by warriors; if attacker has no warriors/pawns left, battle ends. Resolve before-roll effects (attacker orders if both have them), roll: higher die is attacker hits and lower defender hits (equal dice equal); each side's rolled hits are capped by its own warriors, with Alliance defending reversing dice and Vagabond using undamaged swords instead of warriors. Resolve after-roll effects (attacker orders if both), then add extra hits (uncapped) and subtract ignored hits; a defender with no warriors gives attacker one defenseless hit, except Vagabond is defenseless only with no undamaged swords. Each hit removes one opposing piece; hit-taking side chooses its removal order but removes all its warriors before buildings/tokens, and orders effects triggered by removals. Both sides deal counted hits. Whoever removes an enemy building/token scores one VP each, including a defender or a removal outside battle.

answer.part: Crafting costs, reuse, missing item supply, duplicate persistent effects
answer.ruling: The card's bottom-left crafting icons set cost. Marquise, Eyrie, and Alliance activate one matching crafting piece per icon, using the piece's clearing suit; each piece activates only once per turn. Vagabond exhausts one face-up undamaged hammer per icon; its current clearing suit must match every card icon, and it may reuse the pawn but pays a hammer for every icon. An item card cannot be crafted without its corresponding item token in map supply. You cannot craft an identical persistent effect already in your play area.

answer.part: Dominance activation timing, VP threshold, win conditions, and replacing/discarding activated card
answer.ruling: During your own Daylight at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card from hand into your play area, remove your score marker, and stop scoring VP. At the start of your Birdsong, win by ruling three clearings of the matching mouse/rabbit/fox suit, or for bird dominance, two diagonally opposite corner clearings. Meeting the condition earlier does not win immediately. An activated card cannot be removed or replaced. Dominance cards cannot be crafted, but can be spent for suit; when one would enter discard, put it near the map as available instead.

answer.part: Spent dominance destination and taking it, especially bird dominance
answer.ruling: Whenever a dominance card would enter discard, place it near the map as available. During your own Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance card into your hand. Available bird dominance remains bird, so it must be paid for with a bird card; a bird hand card can pay for non-bird dominance. Taking it does not activate it.

answer.part: Two-player deck, hand, ruins/items, and faction setup order
answer.ruling: With two players remove all four dominance cards, shuffle the shared deck, and each player draws three cards. Cover four R building slots with ruins. The map item supply is 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea, 2 coins. Only if Vagabond is present, during its setup hide one each of the R-marked bag, boot, hammer, and sword beneath the four ruins, one per ruin; shuffle the stacks and return them to empty R slots. Without Vagabond, ruins contain no items. Set up factions in letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond; this is distinct from turn order.
answer.evidence: Setup (Standard Setup, steps 3–7); Hidden ruin items

answer.part: Keep placement, Field Hospitals, and rebuilding
answer.ruling: Only Marquise may place pieces in its clearing, but other players may move pieces into it. When any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the keep clearing instead of supply; this can apply outside battle. Without a keep there is no hospital destination. The keep cannot be placed again if removed.
answer.evidence: Marquise de Cat → Keep; Field Hospitals

answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat → Keep; Field Hospitals

answer.part: Marquise Daylight order and actions
answer.ruling: First craft with workshops, then take up to three actions plus one per bird card spent outside an action, in any order/number subject to Recruit's once-per-turn limit. March is one action of up to two moves, which cannot be interrupted to spend a bird or take another action. Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter and is allowed only once per turn. Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill clearing to place one wood there.

answer.part: Marquise Build procedure
answer.ruling: Choose a clearing you rule with an open building slot and building type. Take the leftmost building of that type. Pay the cost atop its column by removing that many wood from the target clearing or other ruled clearings linked to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score VP on the uncovered track space. You need the full wood cost, building, and legal slot; otherwise you cannot build.

answer.part: Eyrie Birdsong and no-roost recovery
answer.ruling: In order: if hand is empty, Emergency Orders draws one card; add one or two hand cards to any Decree columns, with at most one bird card; then if no roosts are on map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all these pieces can be placed.

answer.part: Eyrie Decree resolution
answer.ruling: Craft with roosts first, then resolve every Decree card by column in Recruit → Move → Battle → Build order; choose card order freely within each column. Cards match the suit/location for each action: Recruit a roost clearing (place one warrior at one chosen roost, or Charismatic's two); Move matches origin and requires moving at least one warrior under normal move rules; Battle matches battle clearing and initiates battle there with Eyrie warriors and an enemy; Build matches target and places one roost in a clearing you rule, with an open slot and no roost already there. If any required action cannot be fully completed, immediately Turmoil; do not skip it or continue other columns.
answer.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties → Daylight — resolve the Decree; Decree column table

answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties → Daylight — resolve the Decree

answer.part: Turmoil consequences and remainder of turn
answer.ruling: Lose one VP per bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers; discard every Decree card except Viziers; flip the current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement (if none are face up, flip all leaders face up before choosing); retuck Viziers in the new leader's columns. Daylight ends. Proceed to the normal Evening: score roost track, draw one plus uncovered bonuses, discard to five. Turmoil does not remove map warriors or buildings.

answer.part: Outrage triggers, payment, and no-match/full stack
answer.ruling: Another player triggers Outrage by removing sympathy or moving any warriors into a sympathetic clearing; a moving group costs one matching hand card per affected move, not per warrior. Birds count as matching. If the player has no matching card including birds, they show their hand to Alliance, then Alliance draws a deck card into Supporters. If Supporters is full, discard the incoming card, but the payment or no-match draw still occurs.

answer.part: Revolt and Spread Sympathy timing, eligibility, cost, Martial Law, results
answer.ruling: Complete all Revolts before beginning any Spread Sympathy; each can be done any number of times. Once spreading starts, no return to Revolt that Birdsong. Every supporter spent must match the target clearing; birds are wild. Revolt: choose a sympathetic clearing without a base matching a base still on your board, spend two matching supporters, remove all enemy pieces there, score one VP per enemy building/token, place the matching base, place warriors equal to matching-suit sympathetic clearings including the revolt clearing, and one warrior in Officers. Enemy Vagabond damages three items instead of being removed. Spread Sympathy: choose an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy, or any clearing if none exists; pay supporters shown above the next sympathy token plus one matching supporter if the clearing has at least three warriors of one other player (Martial Law); place token and score uncovered VP. Only one sympathy per clearing; Keep placement ban applies.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Birdsong: Revolt; Spread Sympathy

answer.part: Train, Organize, and losing a base
answer.ruling: Train during Daylight by spending a hand card matching a clearing with a base to place one supply warrior in Officers; Supporters cannot pay. In Evening, Organize is one military operation: remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, place sympathy there, and score uncovered VP; it uses no supporters, has no adjacency or Martial Law cost, but requires legal placement. When a base is removed, discard supporters matching its clearing including birds, remove half officers rounded up, and if no bases remain discard supporters down to five.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Losing a base; Daylight; Evening

answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Losing a base; Daylight; Evening

answer.part: Vagabond Refresh, Slip, normal Move, Rest and Evening draw
answer.ruling: Birdsong Refresh first counts tea already face up on Refresh track: flip two exhausted items per such tea, then three more; tea refreshed now adds no refresh this step. Optional Slip moves to adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, even into hostile warriors, and ignores effects preventing movement out; forest adjacency follows map rules including Winter river. Daylight Move exhausts one boot plus one extra if destination has warriors of any Hostile faction; it ignores rule, cannot enter a forest, and from a forest may move only to adjacent clearing. If in forest at Evening, Rest returns damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up, and ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if able; it does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Always draw one card plus one per face-up coins on track, even after Rest.

answer.part: Explore, Quest, and Repair
answer.ruling: Explore: exhaust torch in ruin's clearing, take its hidden item face up into Satchel or track, score one VP if an item was taken, and remove ruin when its last item is taken, freeing slot. Quest in a matching clearing: choose face-up matching quest, exhaust its two listed items, put it completed in play area, choose VP equal to matching completed quests including this one or draw two cards, then draw replacement quest into public display; no card cost. Repair: exhaust hammer and move one damaged item to Satchel keeping current face; ready tea/coins/bags go to tracks if space.

answer.part: Hostility, Infamy, Aid, and Strike
answer.ruling: Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately makes it Hostile, except the special allied-warrior hit rule. On Vagabond's own turn, battle Infamy scores one extra VP per hostile piece removed, except the warrior that first made that faction Hostile; no Infamy on another player's turn or from Strike. Aid cannot move a Hostile marker out of Hostile, though Aid may still obtain a crafted item. Strike exhausts crossbow to remove one enemy warrior; only if that enemy has no warriors there may it remove another piece of that faction. Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.

answer.part: Coalition eligibility, timing, VP, partner, victory, Hostile partner
answer.ruling: With four or more players, during Vagabond's own Daylight at 10 or more VP, activate dominance to coalition with a player not already in coalition who has the lowest VP among players other than Vagabond (choose among ties). Place score marker on partner's faction board and stop scoring. Vagabond wins if partner wins, including by dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies and coalition does not grant Allied powers; a Hostile partner becomes Indifferent.

answer.part: Precedence and ordinary card versus cannot
answer.ruling: A card overrides Law; Law overrides Learning to Play; faction rules prevail over general rules when incompatible. 'Cannot' is absolute unless explicitly overridden, so an ordinary card does not override a cannot unless it explicitly does so.

answer.part: Unclear simultaneous resolutions and interrupting March
answer.ruling: If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. Marquise March's up-to-two moves are one compound action; do not interrupt it to spend a bird card or take another action.

answer.part: At-start/at-end timing and last step of turn
answer.ruling: 'At start' effects precede all other phase effects; 'at end' effects follow everything else in that phase, before the next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions.

answer.part: Information, deals, card transfers, and consent
answer.ruling: Hand size is public but contents private; reveal/show only when explicitly instructed. Face-up piles may be searched/inspected; deck cannot. Agreements are non-binding; cards may be transferred only as instructed; actions require no consent.
answer.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases → Cards / hand and agreements

answer.part: Empty deck and bird substitutions
answer.ruling: When shared deck empties, immediately shuffle discard into a new deck. Birds substitute for any non-bird suit, including multiple same-suit payments. If instructed to give/discard cards of a non-bird suit, birds count as that suit; a non-bird cannot substitute when bird is explicitly required.

answer.part: Piece shortage, proxies, voluntarily placing fewer, costs and Decree
answer.ruling: Pieces are finite; no proxies. If an instruction cannot place/take/remove all prompted pieces, do the maximum possible and cannot voluntarily do fewer. This does not waive costs or prerequisites and does not waive Eyrie's obligation to complete Decree actions; an uncompletable Decree action causes Turmoil.
answer.evidence: Actions → pieces finite/maximum possible; Eyrie Decree

answer.part: Piece destinations and simultaneous removal effects
answer.ruling: Placed pieces normally come from supply or the leftmost track space; removed tracked pieces normally return to the rightmost empty track space and other faction pieces to supply. Removed items are permanently removed. For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects.
answer.evidence: Actions → Shared rules; Special Rules → Place/remove/replace

answer.part: Forced movement or battle
answer.ruling: Resolve forced actions as if the affected player chose them, retaining that player's abilities and restrictions. A player forced to battle makes its own battle decisions.

answer.part: Enemy replacement in Keep clearing and swap
answer.ruling: Replace requires both removal and placement to be possible; Keep's ban on other players placing pieces in its clearing cannot be bypassed by replacing an enemy piece there. A swap ignores move/place restrictions.

answer.part: Simultaneous 30 VP tie
answer.ruling: If multiple players reach 30 VP simultaneously, the tied player closest clockwise to the current player wins, including the current player.

answer.part: Forest adjacency, Winter river, Fall rule
answer.ruling: Forests are adjacent to clearings touching them without crossing a printed path and to forests separated by just one printed path. Winter's river also divides forests. Fall has no special rules. Vagabond Slip uses this forest adjacency.
answer.evidence: Actions → Shared rules (forest); Vagabond Birdsong → Slip; Overview

answer.part: Marquise setup
answer.ruling: Supply 25 warriors and 8 wood. Put Keep in any corner starting clearing. Put one warrior in every clearing except the diagonally opposite corner. Place one sawmill, workshop, and recruiter among the Keep clearing and adjacent clearings in any combination respecting slots. Put remaining five buildings of each type on tracks from right to left, leaving leftmost space empty.

answer.part: Eyrie setup
answer.ruling: Supply 20 warriors. Place one roost and six warriors in a corner that is not another player's starting corner, diagonally opposite a starting corner if possible. Choose a leader and keep others face up nearby. Tuck the two bird Loyal Viziers into columns listed for that leader. Fill roost track with the other six roosts from right to left.

answer.part: Alliance setup
answer.ruling: Supply 10 warriors; put three bases in matching board spaces and ten sympathy on its track. Draw three additional cards face down into Supporters, separate from its three-card hand. Start with no map pieces or officers.

answer.part: Vagabond setup aside from hidden ruins
answer.ruling: Choose Thief, Tinker, or Ranger and place pawn in any forest. Shuffle quests and display three face up. Take the character's S-marked starting items: tea, coins, and bags go face up on matching tracks; other items go face up in Satchel; return unused S items to box. Put each other faction's relationship marker at Indifferent.

answer.part: Recommended Reach totals and base values
answer.ruling: Recommended minimum total Reach: 17 for two players, 18 for three, 21 for four. Base Reach: Marquise 10, Eyrie 7, Vagabond 5, Alliance 3. The Law permits any mix totaling at least 17 for adventurous groups.

answer.part: Wood production and Evening draw
answer.ruling: Birdsong produces one wood per sawmill in its clearing, limited by the finite supply of eight wood. Daylight Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill clearing to place one wood there; both methods use the same supply. Evening draws one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discards down to five.

answer.part: Recruit shortage choice
answer.ruling: Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter. If supply cannot fill all recruiters, place the maximum available, choosing among eligible recruiters.

answer.part: Eyrie item craft scoring and Builder
answer.ruling: Eyrie crafted items score one VP instead of the printed VP under Disdain for Trade; other extra crafting-point effects still apply. Builder ignores Disdain for Trade.
answer.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties → Lords of the Forest / Disdain for Trade; Leader table

answer.part: Eyrie leaders and Viziers/abilities
answer.ruling: Builder: Recruit and Move Viziers; ignores Disdain for Trade. Charismatic: Recruit and Battle; each Recruit places two warriors instead of one. Commander: Move and Battle; one extra hit as attacker. Despot: Move and Build; when removing at least one enemy building/token in battle, score one extra VP beyond normal removal points.

answer.part: Charismatic Recruit with only one warrior remaining
answer.ruling: No. Charismatic must place two warriors for each Recruit card; if the required action cannot be fully completed because only one remains, immediately enter Turmoil. The maximum-placement rule does not excuse the Eyrie's obligation to complete Decree actions.
answer.evidence: Eyrie Decree Recruit; Turmoil; maximum possible rule

answer.part: Guerrilla War dice and warrior limit
answer.ruling: When Alliance defends, Alliance uses the higher die and attacker the lower. Warrior caps on rolled hits still apply; Guerrilla War does not bypass them.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Guerrilla War; Battle roll

answer.part: Supporters use/inspection/hand limit
answer.ruling: Alliance may inspect its face-down Supporters stack. Supporters can be spent only for suit, not for crafting; they are separate from hand cards and do not count toward the hand limit.

answer.part: Spread then Revolt in same Birdsong
answer.ruling: No. All Revolts must be completed before starting Spread Sympathy. Once spreading starts, you cannot return to Revolt that Birdsong, so newly spread sympathy cannot support a same-Birdsong Revolt.

answer.part: Martial Law with two opponents at two warriors each and Organize cost
answer.ruling: No Martial Law: the chosen clearing must have at least three warriors of one other player; two players with two each do not meet that condition. Martial Law adds one matching supporter to Spread Sympathy. Organize has no Martial Law cost.

answer.part: Outrage from placing, pawn movement, and accompanying allied warriors
answer.ruling: Placing warriors in sympathy does not trigger Outrage, and moving only the Vagabond pawn does not trigger it. Moving any warriors into sympathy does trigger Outrage; therefore allied warriors accompanying the pawn trigger it. The mover adds one matching card per affected move, not per warrior.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Outrage; Vagabond Allied benefits

answer.part: Alliance Evening operations and draw
answer.ruling: Take military operations up to the number of officers, in any order and repetition. An operation does not consume an officer. After operations, draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard down to five.

answer.part: One Recruit operation
answer.ruling: One Recruit operation places one warrior at one clearing with a base.

answer.part: Vagabond pawn under revolt/remove-all effect
answer.ruling: The Vagabond pawn cannot be removed. If an enemy effect removes all enemy pieces from its clearing, instead damage three Vagabond items.
answer.evidence: Vagabond → Pawn and items; Alliance Revolt

answer.part: Vagabond hits, defenseless status, exhausted swords, excess hits
answer.ruling: Vagabond's rolled-hit maximum, attacking or defending, equals all undamaged swords in Satchel, face up or face down, so exhausted undamaged swords count. As defender it is defenseless only with no undamaged swords. Vagabond takes hits as item damage; a hit damages one undamaged item of its choice, and excess hits are ignored when no undamaged items remain.
answer.evidence: Battle → Roll/Count/Deal; Vagabond → Pawn and items; Daylight Battle

answers.evidence: Battle; Vagabond → Battle; Pawn and items

answer.part: Tea/coins/bags tracks and payment
answer.ruling: Face-up tea/coins/bags in Satchel immediately move to an empty matching track space if possible; each track holds at most three of its type. Exhausting a track item moves it to Satchel. Damaged items cannot pay actions even if face up; action costs require a face-up undamaged item.

answer.part: Capacity, counted items, timing, and excess
answer.ruling: Satchel plus Damaged box capacity is six items plus two per face-up bag on its track. Track items do not count toward load. Check capacity in Evening's final step, not immediately upon acquiring items; permanently remove chosen Satchel/Damaged items until within limit.

answer.part: Forest Rest versus Refresh/Repair
answer.ruling: Forest Rest returns all damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up, and moves ready tea/coins/bags to tracks if able. It does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Refresh flips exhausted items face up according to tea and the three-item refresh; Repair exhausts a hammer and moves one damaged item to Satchel keeping its current face.
answer.evidence: Vagabond → Birdsong Refresh; Daylight Repair; Evening Rest

answer.part: Aid cost/target/item and relationship advancement
answer.ruling: Aid exhausts any one undamaged face-up item and gives a card matching the Vagabond's clearing to a player with faction pieces there, including Hostile. A crafted item is not required; the Vagabond may then take one item from that player's Crafted Items box, but no available item is required to Aid. To advance a non-Hostile relationship one space, Aid that faction the number of times printed between current and next spaces in the same turn; each Aid counts toward only one improvement. Advance and score the new space's VP; at Allied, each later Aid scores two VP.

answer.part: Allied Aid/movement/attacking and own-faction restriction
answer.ruling: At Allied, each subsequent Aid scores two VP. On a move, Vagabond may force warriors of one Allied faction to accompany pawn to destination; those warriors obey their own movement restrictions, cannot accompany a move specified to be alone, and moving them into sympathy triggers Outrage. At start of battle as attacker, Vagabond may treat warriors of one Allied faction there as its own; rolled-hit cap equals those warriors plus all its undamaged swords. They can join against a different enemy, but cannot be used to attack that ally itself.

answer.part: When ally becomes Hostile from taking hits
answer.ruling: In a battle where Vagabond uses Allied warriors as its own, it may absorb hits by removing those warriors or damaging items. At battle end, the ally becomes Hostile only if more allied warriors were removed than items Vagabond damaged in that battle; equal numbers do not trigger it.
answer.evidence: Vagabond → Taking hits with an ally

answers.evidence: Vagabond → Taking hits with an ally

answer.part: Mixed-suit card, repeated pawn crafting, immediate item use
answer.ruling: Vagabond cannot craft a card requiring fox and rabbit icons from one clearing, because its current clearing must match every icon. It may activate the pawn repeatedly, but exhausts a separate hammer per icon. A crafted item can immediately be taken face up into Satchel or a track.

answer.part: Base Vagabond characters and special actions
answer.ruling: Thief starts boot, torch, tea, sword; Steal exhausts torch to take a random hand card from a player with faction pieces in the clearing. Tinker starts boot, torch, bag, hammer; Day Labor exhausts torch to take a discard-pile card matching the clearing (bird always qualifies). Ranger starts boot, torch, crossbow, sword; Hideout exhausts torch to repair three items keeping their faces, immediately ends Daylight and begins Evening.

answer.part: Ruin after last item and ordinary construction
answer.ruling: Removing a ruin's last item during Explore removes the ruin and frees its building slot. Ruins block building slots and can be removed only when explicitly allowed, so ordinary building placement cannot remove one.

answer.part: Coalition partner as enemy and Allied powers
answer.ruling: Coalition partners are not enemies and coalition does not itself grant Allied relationship powers.

answer.part: Vagabond battle VP calculation
answer.ruling: Total is 3 VP: 0 ordinary VP for the first warrior, which makes the faction Hostile and is exempt from Infamy; 0 ordinary VP plus 1 Infamy for the second hostile warrior; 1 ordinary VP for the building plus 1 Infamy for removing that hostile building in battle on Vagabond's own turn. Thus removal points are 1 and Infamy points are 2.
answer.evidence: Vagabond → Hostile/Infamy; Scoring → Ordinary removal VP

answer.part: Vagabond normal movement boot cost by hostile destination
answer.ruling: Into a clearing with only hostile buildings/tokens, exhaust one boot. Into a clearing containing hostile warriors, exhaust one boot plus one extra boot, regardless of how many hostile factions' warriors are there.

answer.part: Taking dominance and action allowance
answer.ruling: Taking an available dominance card puts it into hand; it does not activate it. Taking and activating are separate and neither requires a faction action allowance.

answer.part: Faction-piece ownership and items
answer.ruling: Faction-piece ownership cannot change: each player owns its chosen faction and listed faction pieces, except items. Items are not faction pieces or enemy pieces, and possessing one does not make it faction-owned.

answer.part: Immediate and persistent crafting cards; use from play area
answer.ruling: Resolve an immediate-effect card then discard the crafting card. Keep persistent-effect card in play area and gain its text; it is outside hand and cannot be spent, discarded, or used for another purpose unless explicitly instructed. You cannot craft an identical persistent effect already in play.

answer.part: Ambush/dominance crafting and other uses
answer.ruling: Neither Ambush nor Dominance cards can be crafted. Defender may play a matching Ambush (birds wild) for two immediate hits, or attacker may play a matching Ambush to foil a defending ambush. Dominance may be activated to change victory condition or spent for suit.

answer.part: Starting player, seating, score markers, dice, setup order
answer.ruling: Choose starting player and seating randomly. Set score markers at 0; put battle dice nearby. Faction setup is in letter order Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond and is distinct from turn order.

answer.part: When ordinary 30 VP victory takes effect
answer.ruling: The first player to reach 30 wins immediately, on any player's turn; they need not finish the action, phase, or turn.

answer.part: Battle initiation requirements
answer.ruling: Choose a clearing containing your warriors or pawn and an enemy there as defender. You need not rule the clearing.

answer.part: Order of battle effects
answer.ruling: Attacker chooses order of applicable before-roll effects when both players have them, and likewise after-roll effects. The side taking hits chooses the order of effects triggered by its own pieces' removal.

answer.part: Ignore hits in Count Hits
answer.ruling: In Count Hits, add extra hits (which are uncapped by warriors), then subtract ignored hits.

answer.part: Non-Vagabond item craft destination and VP
answer.ruling: The corresponding item token comes from map item supply and goes to the crafting faction's Crafted Items box; the crafting card is discarded if immediate effect. Score VP printed on the item card, except Eyrie scores one VP under Disdain for Trade (Builder ignores this). Vagabond can immediately take the item face up into Satchel/track.
answer.evidence: Actions → Craft; separate component table; Eyrie Disdain

answer.part: Eyrie/Alliance crafting pieces, suit, question mark
answer.ruling: Eyrie activates roosts; Alliance activates sympathy. Each piece's suit is its clearing's suit. A three-color question-mark icon accepts any suit.

answer.part: Mobilize and ordering Daylight actions
answer.ruling: Mobilize adds a hand card to Supporters, respecting the cap. Alliance may take Craft, Mobilize, and Train in any order and number during Daylight; it need not finish crafting before mobilizing or training.

answer.part: Eyrie Evening score/draw and Turmoil
answer.ruling: In Evening score VP on the rightmost empty roost-track space, draw one card plus uncovered draw bonuses, and discard down to five. This full normal Evening still occurs after Turmoil.

answer.part: Vagabond Battle action payment
answer.ruling: Exhaust one sword to initiate the Daylight Battle action. An exhausted undamaged sword cannot pay, even though face-down undamaged swords count toward Vagabond's rolled-hit maximum; payment requires a face-up undamaged item.
answer.evidence: Vagabond → Pawn and items; Daylight Battle

answer.part: Turn phase sequence and next player
answer.ruling: Turns proceed clockwise through Birdsong, Daylight, Evening. After a player's Evening, the next player clockwise takes their turn.

answer.part: Item hit selection and damage
answer.ruling: A hit damages one undamaged item of Vagabond's choice, moving it to Damaged box without changing its face. Already-damaged items cannot absorb another hit; excess hits are ignored when no undamaged items remain.

answer.part: Alliance Evening operation count
answer.ruling: Alliance may take military operations up to its number of officers, in any order and repetition; operations do not consume officers.

answer.part: One Recruit operation
answer.ruling: Place one warrior at one clearing with a base.

answer.part: Vagabond Daylight action allowance/order/repetition
answer.ruling: Vagabond may take Daylight actions in any order and number as ready undamaged items permit; action types may be repeated, subject to their item costs/requirements.

answer.part: Strike cost and eligible item
answer.ruling: Strike exhausts one crossbow to remove an enemy warrior in the clearing; only if that enemy has no warriors there may you remove another of its faction pieces. The crossbow must be face-up and undamaged to pay; exhausted or damaged crossbows cannot pay.
answer.evidence: Vagabond → Pawn and items; Daylight Strike

answers.evidence: Vagabond → Pawn and items; Daylight Strike
